Chapter 7: Finding Humor in the Unexpected.
If there’s one thing the coast will teach you, it’s this—plans almost never go the way you expect. The weather? Changes in a heartbeat. Boats decide to break down at the absolute worst moment. And even the most carefully planned lobster bake can spiral into chaos... and somehow, that’s where the laughter really kicks in.
Picture this: It’s a bright summer afternoon and a group of friends are off for a picnic on a little island. The sky’s clear, everyone’s excited, and the boat is packed with food and supplies. But halfway across the bay, the engine coughs... then dies. Suddenly, they’re just drifting. At first, there’s frustration—missed lunches, sunburns, all the stuff that could go wrong. But then, something shifts. Someone starts spinning stories, another pulls out a harmonica, and before long, they’re belting out old sea shanties, their voices echoing over the water.
When help finally arrives, the rescue is met with cheers—and plenty of good-natured, self-mocking jokes. The picnic still happens, just a little later, and somehow, it’s even better for the adventure. Looking back, nobody talks about the sandwiches. It’s the mishap they remember—and laugh about.
Somewhere else, there’s a local teacher who’s planned a big field trip to the tide pools. But the bus? It takes a wrong turn and ends up miles from the coast. The kids are restless, maybe a little let down. But the teacher rallies them for an impromptu scavenger hunt in a nearby meadow. And guess what? That unexpected day becomes one of their favorite memories.
Most people dread the unexpected, don’t they? See it as something to get past. But around here, the ability to laugh at life’s curveballs is almost an art. The coast is full of stories just like these—weddings rained out, fishing trips cut short by fog, holiday feasts suddenly interrupted by a power outage. In every case, it’s the shared laughter and quick thinking that turn disappointment into something delightful.
There’s a quiet wisdom in this mindset. When you let go of trying to control every detail, you open up space for joy to show up in the most surprising ways. The unexpected becomes an invitation—a chance to play, to improvise, to connect with others in ways you never saw coming.
So as the sun sets, and the sound of laughter drifts across the water, it’s a gentle reminder. Life’s always going to be unpredictable. But with a sense of humor, the journey is so much sweeter.
